text_fidelity_a:
Fire 7 Kids tablet, 7" Display, ages 3-7, 16 GB, (2019 release), Blue Kid-Proof Case We wanted to love this, like talk ourselves into tolerating it love this. At its root, it’s a great idea! The case is a nice added feature and the FreeTime program is great. I like that the majority of the content is child friendly, but at the same time, my little ones can download stuff willy nilly, which creates clutter. I do not like the formatting or the controls. We endlessly swipe through apps or have to search it once it’s gone from the Recently Opened tab. There’s no true “home screen” where you have your apps laid out. Instead, it’s very similar to browsing Netflix, which is something I do not want in a tablet. The controls are a joke and some are difficult to navigate. The swipe down controls are always accessible, letting my littles always get into mischief like disconnecting the internet, dimming the screen so low I can’t see it to fix, and turning on the sleep mode color way. There is no way to pin the screen to a specific app (like guided access to keep the tablet on Netflix during a long car ride) and there is no way to create dead zones so controls can’t be messed with. The lock button is small and easily missed being lumped in with all the other buttons. We often find ourselves frustrated with the entire device.

We loved the concept and the warranty behind the device. That is the sole reason we are keeping it. However, it is frustrating to use. We much prefer an iPad where we can hand select content and use features like guided access.
text_fidelity_b: Fire 7 Kids tablet, 7" Display, ages 3-7, 16 GB, (2019 release), Blue Kid-Proof Case

Each of these machines gets 4 gig dedicated ram, and I leave the last 4 for the host OS. This RAM has held up to that kind of intense use without any problem. I am delighted.

I also use this machine for intense gaming, and again, this RAM does an awesome job. The memory, left at default configuration, is fast, fast, fast. Again, I'm a happy user.

Overall, I think the product is an exceptional value -- a top performer at a sensible price. The best I can say is, after a while you won't notice it. It will give you solid performance with no problems, and will just become invisible as you. I will definitely be using them again next time I'm in the market for memory.

The connection to the stereo can be done via a single cable or using a two cable (L/R) setup. Cables for both options are included. I'm using the L/R option, and plugged the cables into the TAPE input on my stereo receiver.

The sound quality is excellent. It is very hard to tell the difference in quality when streaming audio via this receiver versus playing a CD on the receiver. Movie dialog was outstanding as well.

The fact that it does not require a battery is a plus and a minus. On the plus side, no need to worry about recharging or swapping batteries. On the down side, it was a bit of a problem for me to get the cables routed since the wall outlet near my stereo is not easily accessible. I wound up running a short extension cord so that I could plug in the receiver close enough to the stereo so that the L/R cables would reach.

As a bonus, it includes a USB port so you can use it to recharge your phone/tablet/etc.

That one minor issue aside, I'm very impressed with the performance of this product. Highly recommend.

text_fidelity_a:
Canon Office Products MG5420 Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner and Copier I've had problems with Pixmas in the past, mostly having to do with wireless networks and having to reinstall the software over and over to try to get them to hang on to network settings. I can't guarantee that this printer is going to be any better in the long run, but the set-up actually works pretty well if you use the standard version, not the WPS... and I'm getting way ahead of myself on this one.

To begin with, the printer requires a lot of time for set-up. You're not going to be doing this on the fly, so set aside an hour or so to: 1) remove all the tape of which there is much, 2) read over the instructions 3) install the ink, 4) run a print alignment 5) set up your wireless connection (about which more in a moment) 6) install the software (which takes a good 15 minutes or more), and 7) put the machine (and yourself) through its paces. Yeah, it's going to take a while.

Now I know you can read about the features on your own, so I'm here to tell you about the things that work for me and those that don't. First off, the wireless set-up is confusing. Choose Standard instead of WPS and save yourself some headaches unless you're a computer whiz kid. After the third error message in the WPS set-up I went to standard, entered my pass code and had the connection up and running in about a minute.

Once that was done and the software was installed I fired up the Canon Image Garden. First I scanned an image and attempted to rotate, crop and fix any deficiencies I found. The scan was over sharp and looked a bit jagged, but a little fiddling with the Canon software fixed that. Canon software also rotated and cropped perfectly. One really nice feature is that they remind you to put the printing side of the paper down in the paper cassette. How many pieces of paper will that save?

The biggest complaint I had was that it didn't give me a choice of which paper cassette to use for printing, so I got a ridiculously truncated image on the first try. I believe it chooses the paper based on the size of the image, which I get, but at the same time that limits flexibility in printing. I opened another photo processing program and it allowed me to print from whatever cassette I liked. Coupled with a better suite of applications for correction and enhancement, I think it's safe to say that I'll be using the Canon software almost never.

Printing on plain paper is clearly not going to be as satisfactory as it is on glossy, but in some cases I found it surprisingly good, good enough to give you an idea of what sort of image you're going to end up with when you switch to photo paper. It's also more than good enough for printing out emails and web pages.

Scanning and printing are both pretty fast, another plus. And the copy function works pretty seamlessly without any sort of computer interface. Just punch a couple of buttons and Bob's your uncle! It does take a bit of time to warm up and is a little noisy but no more so than any Canon printer I've ever used. It's not bothersome, in my opinion. You might feel otherwise.

Inks are easy to install, but you'll find refills pricey, no question. I suspect off-brand ones are available or will be soon enough.

In short, it's a good, inexpensive printer for a home or home office. Use photo paper and settings and get the full quality the MG5420 is capable of producing; I think it's pretty remarkable. The photos I printed out are as good as or in one case, better than the original. That's a powerful recommendation in my book.
text_fidelity_b: Canon Office Products MG5420 Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner and Copier

The same is true for the main arm which holds up the crossbar. I’m still a little leery that it’s going to start slipping after a while, but for now, I think it’s probably secure. I will say that the clamp and main post are heavy duty and feel very sturdy. Also, the arms are easy to move and reposition side to side and back and forth. I also like that I was able to mount the monitors without a second person, due to the assisting bolts where you can “hang” the monitor on the bracket until you get everything screwed tight (like a ceiling fan).

Overall 4 stars due to my hands and arms are going to be sore tomorrow due to all the required tightening.

text_fidelity_a:
WiFi Video Projector, WEWATCH V10B Wireless Portable Movie Projector with Bluetooth Full HD 1080P Supported Home Theater Video Projector Compatible with HDMI, VGA, TV Stick, iPhone, Android The WEWATCH V30 Portable Projector is a good 1080p projector for its size. I watched some movies with the screen setup to 80-90 inches and the picture looked very good in a dark room. It's important to watch this projector in low ambient lighting due to its low ANSI lumens, as bright light will wash out the picture.

The size of the projector is not as small as the pictures make it seem. Though it is not advertised as a pico projector, I expected it to be smaller. With that said, the projector is not so large that it would be hard to transport or store when not in use.

Unfortunately, I was not able to get the Wi-Fi feature to work with my Iphone. This is not a dealbreaker for me, as I plugged a Roku stick into the HDMI port and the system worked well.

I was surprised by how good the native speakers sound. I found watching movies enjoyable and voices were easy to hear. There are adjustments for the bass and treble levels in the menus. The unit has a headphone jack in the rear which makes hooking up an external speaker set up a breeze.

The fan on the unit is very quiet and is not distracting while it is in use.

While I really like this projector, there is a large downside. The lack of keystone correction is a huge oversight. Placing this projector without keystone adjustment means the projector has to be directly in line with the viewing area making it necessary to use a tripod in most instances. Having to bring a tripod along, makes the unit less portable.

Overall, this is a small projector with a great picture, as long as you can place it in the perfect location without much ambient lighting. If WEWATCH added keystone correction and refined the mirroring feature, this would be a 5 star projector.
text_fidelity_b: WiFi Video Projector, WEWATCH V10B Wireless Portable Movie Projector with Bluetooth Full HD 1080P Supported Home Theater Video Projector Compatible with HDMI, VGA, TV Stick, iPhone, Android

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Galaxy Tab (7-inch, 16GB, Wi-Fi) I really liked this 7" Tab (GT-P1010) at first. It's most useful function is web surfing.

Now, after several months of use, it's SLOOOOOOOW to load and update pages and locks up occasionally for no particular reason. I've uninstalled every unnecessary app but whether using the default Browser or Dolphin, it's more frustrating than useful.

It's also inaccurate for when inputting via keyboard. Oftentimes the keyboard adds wild characters all by itself.

Forget firmware updates. You are stuck with whatever it came with. And if you think Samsung will be any help, think again. I put "GT-P1010" in Samsung's product support page and got "no results."

I have to say Apple's major firmware updates work a whole lot better. First, because they happen at all and second, because they are seamless and reliable. Android is buggy and needs fixing on this Samsung Tablet. Samsung's "answer" is to buy a new tablet.

The device has two cameras and would be ideal for video chatting, but won't work with Skype. Apparently it needs the next version of Android. (See above concerning that impossibility.) But who knows if the next-up model will work either?

These things all want to be Apple but simply fall short.

One nice thing is that most Flash content is supported when web surfing. Apple is way lacking here. I used an iPad 1 for some time and it's pretty frustrating that it simply ignores so much content.

Bottom line is I won't buy another wannabe Samsung device like this that lacks firmware updates. (I did the same thing looking for the perfect mp3 player: everyone tried to sell the "iPod killer" and I spent more money trying to avoid the iPod. Then I bought an iPod3 and later an iPhone4 and understood how excellent their engineering and software and OS are and how with OS updates the devices continually get better even after you make the purchase.) They are too expensive to throw away and Samsung can't or won't fix the bugs. Thus you are stuck with an expensive, buggy toy that's frustrating to use. No thank you.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Galaxy Tab (7-inch, 16GB, Wi-Fi)

text_fidelity_a:
Lexar E-Series 128GB Micro SD Card 2 Pack, microSDXC UHS-I Flash Memory Card with Adapter, 100MB/s, C10, U3, A1, V30, Full HD, 4K UHD, High Speed TF Card I've owned a few Lexar USB drives and Micro USB drives in the past and they have all had good quality and performance. I've attached the crystal diskmark performance below, but keep in mind that I am using the built-in microsd reader in my computer so speeds may vary as the reader has just as much to do with these benchmarks as the memory card itself.

I don't have any equipment that really stresses the microsd too much. The cameras that I have, while they can record up to 4K at 30fps, have generally had no problem writing to a U1 microsd. The Lexar, which I keep in my Osmo Pocket, is no exception, it has not had an issue recording video.

There is one key thing to point out about Lexar storage media that I've experienced in two of my past devices and that is the built-in expiration or time-bomb (if you don't agree with this philosophy). Lexar seems to have the philosophy that keeping your data intact is the most important when it comes to these products. Solid-state storage media has a theoretical limit to how many times they can be written to. Once that is hit, the media will be permanently damaged. Lexar has written into their firmware, a hard limit that once you write a certain number of times to their media, it will become read-only, keeping your data intact, but the storage unusable from that point on.

While I've experienced failed media in the past, I really only had this behavior with Lexar. I have to say, it did save my wife from losing the pictures on her phone if the card failed instead of becoming read-only.
text_fidelity_b: Lexar E-Series 128GB Micro SD Card 2 Pack, microSDXC UHS-I Flash Memory Card with Adapter, 100MB/s, C10, U3, A1, V30, Full HD, 4K UHD, High Speed TF Card

Like the other two, this is a little larger than initially expected, but it has to be to have all the built-in adapters. There is still no Italy plug or ground conductor, so this is only ideal if you only have an ungrounded device like a computer (again, without ground) and a few USB-chargeable devices like phones and cameras.

This one has a USB-C port, unlike one of my others, but - unlike the one I have that does have USB-C - the total current is more limited. Both adapters with USB-C ports only support 5v output, so they may not charge your device if your device can only accept higher voltage (USB-C has multiple layers of standards, so can be a bit confusing).

I like this adapter when traveling to multiple regions within one trip. Otherwise, I'll just use the cheap adapters which by themselves are smaller. Out of the three I own, I'm not sure which is best; I think it depends on your personal situation. Hopefully I shared enough to help you decide.

MEE audio M6 X1 Wired In-Ear Sports Headphones with Microphone and Remote – Sweatproof Secure Fit Earphones for Running, Jogging, and Gym Workouts (Black) (EP-X1-GYBK) Even pre break-in, these sounded great: probably the best headphones under $20 I've found. After break-in, these MEE buds were sounding like something that cost 4-5 times as much with a nice, even frequency response that favors bass only slightly. I find them comparable to $60-$80 Sennheisers, my previous favorites (which superseded Sony and Koss buds that I also liked). These MEE buds came with 3 sets (S, M, and L) of your typical soft rubber earpieces as well as 2 sets of the interesting multi-tiered earpieces shown in the photos and a pretty standard cloth case. Between the various earpiece options, it's unlikely anyone will have an issue finding a good fit.

The cord is about 1 m long, which suits my purposes. I like the over-the-ear wire bits, too, as they prevent tugs on the cord from dislodging them. They might be awkward with some kinds of glasses, but my straight-earpiece sunglasses fit over them fine. They can be bent to hang down more like normal earbuds if desired, though.

I'll be checking out more MEE products now, seeing what a great value these were. I still favor AKG and Beyerdynamic at the high end, but for my biking/hiking/running/workout listening needs, I'll probably be coming back to MEE.
text_fidelity_b: MEE audio M6 X1 Wired In-Ear Sports Headphones with Microphone and Remote – Sweatproof Secure Fit Earphones for Running, Jogging, and Gym Workouts (Black) (EP-X1-GYBK)

text_fidelity_a:
ARCTIC S111 USB-Powered Portable Stereo Speakers for Tablet/eReader/MP3/Computers, Balanced Treble/Superior Bass - Blue Note: I would love to love this speaker set, but it has inconsistent performance with various devices. I received a review sample and was pleased by the sound when I plugged this into the phone port on my ThinkPad T61. The sound was clear and I could hear every note on the album that I use to test speakers (Miles Davis' [[ASIN:B000002ADT Kind of Blue]]). I use that album because the instruments in the ensemble cover low, mid and high range frequencies. The bass was a little thin, but with the speakers less than two feet away the sound was rich and I was happy.

Where I started to experience problems was when I plugged this into the 3.5mm port on my Samsung Galaxy Note 3 phone. There was static in the mix. The same with my [[ASIN:B00D029NNA Samsung Galaxy Tab 3 10.1 inch]] - static interfered with the music. My final test was to plug the 3.5mm cable end into an [[ASIN:B00AEJJRBK Avantree Cara Bluetooth 4.0 Handsfree stereo Car Kit with mic]] and connect via bluetooth. The sound was crystal clear.

I am not sure what conclusions to draw. It could be something wrong with the Samsung phone and tablet, although both work perfectly with headphones which I have directly plugged into their 3.5mm ports. It may be that the 3.5mm cable and interface on the input of this speaker is overly sensitive to impedance and the slightest deviation will induce static. I am not sure, but because I was unable to get the same quality consistently across all devices with which I tested these speakers I subtracted two stars.

Construction is exceptional, although I wish the design employed removable USB and 3.5mm cables instead of the fixed ones that provide power and signal inputs, and connect the two units. As it stands if a cable breaks it will take some skill to repair it. With removable, off-the-shelf cables a broken one can be rectified with a trip to an electronics store.

Overall, on the two devices that I tested with which these speakers worked the sound was spectacular. On the other two it was unlistenable. If you are connecting this to a bluetooth receiver it's probably a safe choice, but if you are connecting this to anything else I would proceed with caution.
text_fidelity_b: ARCTIC S111 USB-Powered Portable Stereo Speakers for Tablet/eReader/MP3/Computers, Balanced Treble/Superior Bass - Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Oasis E-reader (Previous Generation - 9th) – Graphite, 7" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Waterproof, Built-In Audible, 32 GB, Wi-Fi - with Special Offers (Closeout) I purchased one of these 9th generation Kindle Oasis. The first unit I received would freeze during the configuration process. You could reset it, but if you try to configure, it would freeze again. At this point, I made the mistake of asking for a replacement instead of just returning the faulty Kindle Oasis for a refund. A replacement unit arrived in three days. Unfortunately, the replacement unit was DoA. There was a fixed image on screen, and I wasn't able to get a response from this Kindle after charging it for a long time and multiple reset attempts. I had already shipped the first unit back using a UPS shipping label created by Amazon at this point. I went to my Amazon Orders page to return the second unit for a credit. But Amazon web interface wouldn't allow a self service return for refund. I had contact customer service and deal with several customer service representatives. They consistently asked me to try some simple trouble shooting steps ( most of which are not even applicable if you have a completely dead kindle). They wouldn't listen to me when I said I just wanted to return it, and try to pressure me into another replacement. At this point, I had spent several hours troubleshooting, talking to Amazon Customer service, taking packages to UPS, etc. so I insisted on a return for refund. This time, the customer service representative said he was having problems generating the return label, and then disappeared. After several minutes of wait, another customer rep took over and worked on this case for another 10 minutes or so. At that point, I ended up with two sets of return labels in my email. The customer service rep told me to use the labels from the second email (in chronological order). So the next day, I shipped the replacement Kindle Oasis back. A few days later, I saw on UPS tracking that the package was delivered to Amazon and three days after this I received an email confirmation from Amazon that my first return was received. A few days later, I saw on UPS tracking that the second Kindle Oasis (replacement) was also received by Amazon. I waited a few days for return confirmation and refund from Amazon, but nothing happened. When I contacted Amazon Customer service, they kept telling me that I shouldn't worry about getting charged as my replacement is complete. But they could see no record of my return of the replacement. I spent probably a good half an hour chatting with a customer service rep but they couldn't help me at all since they could only see the record for on return request. That chat ended with no resolution because I ran out of time and had to get to an appointment. Later, I got in touch with yet another service rep, and explained everything from scratch. Luckily, that person was able to find records of both returns being received by Amazon and finally issued me a refund.

So lessons from this story:
1. Don't buy a 9th gen Kindle Oasis. There seems to be serious quality control issues. The probability of one customer receiving two faulty Kindles in a row would be infinitesimal unless fault rates are in the 20% range.
2. If you receive a faulty Kindle from Amazon, return it for a refund. Don't ask for a replacement. Amazon's automated return process cannot handle the return of a replacement unit, and you will sink a lot of time dealing with customer service representatives
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Oasis E-reader (Previous Generation - 9th) – Graphite, 7" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Waterproof, Built-In Audible, 32 GB, Wi-Fi - with Special Offers (Closeout)

CoolBELL 17.3 Inches Convertible Laptop Messenger Bag Shoulder Bag Backpack Oxford Cloth Multi-Functional Briefcase for Men Women Laptop/MacBook (Blue) First and foremost, I need a convertible backpack which allows for transport - all materials needed for the long days on campus (grad student). In addition, I need the professional aspect to function as a briefcase. Solely on those points, this bag fits the bill. (BTW - no discount or freebie here for this review - I paid for this!)
PROS:
1. Material: feels and looks professional, good color, seems at the very least to be water repellent
2. Zippers: seem strong enough, especially when loaded - two of them house the briefcase handles
3. Padding: quality - on the backpack straps and particularly the section directly meant for the computer
4. Compartments: although the pictures do not necessarily show this, there are zippers on the outside, and inside, a pocket with divisions for pencils/pens/highlighters.

CONS:
1. Backpack adjustable straps: are on the lower part not allowing for easy adjustment while on your back
2. Lower connection backpack straps: hidden - cannot see whether sewn in well or not
3. Strap to hold computer in place: oddly long, which would allow for movement and sliding around, something you don't want your computer to do when inside
4. No compartment/pocket for a water bottle (my pet peeve)
5. PRIMARY (HUGE) ISSUE: Backpack straps which rest on upper trapezoids (left and right) are situated in a very uncomfortable position when fully loaded. I'm unsure if it's the angle or the placement, but the straps are too close to your neck and would cause pain. Primarily for this reason, I'm returning the backpack. Sad because even with the other cons (more annoyances than anything else) if it were not for this one, I would've kept the backpack because the pros outweigh the cons.

Pictures: It's important to see how a backpack will perform in my daily life. Therefore, the pictures provide a sense of how much stuff this can carry, with the contents both packed and unpacked.

Contents: Lenovo ThinkPad T460 in neoprene case, keys, 1 1/2" loose-leaf binder, yearly planner, scientific calculator, computer power cord, small cosmetic case, large cosmetic bag which houses pens/pencils/highlighters/usb drive/mouse/headphones and wallet.

Final thoughts: if only used as a briefcase/shoulder bag, this may be for you. However, if the primary purpose is to function as a backpack, good luck. I think another reviewer mentioned the oddly-placed backpack straps, but sadly, I ignored that advice.
In addition, cannot ascertain the strength of the shoulder strap as I didn't want to break the seal, but it is pictured.

ZUMIMALL Security Cameras Wireless Outdoor-2K Home Security Camera Battery Powered, Outdoor Security Cameras with 3MP Color Night Vision/Spotlight/IP66 Waterproof/PIR Detection/2-Way Talk/Cloud/SD I have been testing and reviewing WiFi cameras for the last five years. Over that time the industry has seen major advances which has led to incredible availability of high quality cameras at very reasonable costs. I have tested nearly 100 cameras and it takes a bit to impress me but I must say this set did just that.

I had no problem setting this camera up on my network. I set it both up after fully charging them in about a half hour with no issues.

Due to security precautions I never use cloud based storage in relation to WiFi cameras because that amount of constant data transfer opens your network to unnecessary hacking. The only cameras that I employ in my home allow for local storage - whether to a dedicated hard drive or individual micro SD held within each camera. This camera can hold up to a 128GB micro SD card. The card will over write the oldest data first - how much footage the card holds is dictated by the settings you select. Due to the fact these cameras only record when motion is detected a 128GB card will hold quite a lot and should suffice for 99% of people.

It’s important to know that by default the camera is set to record and save to the cloud. That can easily be reset in preference settings. In addition if you don’t install a micro SD card your camera will only capture still images when viewing - if you don’t have two extra micro SD cards order two when purchasing this set.

The camera provides a crystal clear 1080p footage and I found the motion activation very responsive. With my mesh WiFi network I encountered no lag in viewing - typically camera lag has to do with individual network properties rather than the camera itself.

The batteries in these cameras are phenomenal and actually last as long as is claimed in the listing. The battery’s life will be dictated by how often the camera is activated by motion but I have had both cameras installed and running now for over 2 months without having to recharge yet.

In my tests I found this to be an excellent budget friendly WiFi camera set that as long as you utilize the micro SD card feature is quite secure. Not having to run power cables is a major advantage and will allow these to be placed in far more places. The internal batteries are excellent and are sure to impress. The app is well designed, intuitive and easy to use even for beginners.

This is an all around excellent set of wireless WiFi cameras that I have recommended and do to you as well.

Thanks for reading my review. I enjoy writing them as I value reading other’s reviews when I’m making a buying decision. I regularly update my reviews to reflect any changes I may discover and to include helpful tips you may need if you purchase the product. I will always make every effort to answer any questions I can as it is my pleasure to help.
text_fidelity_b: ZUMIMALL Security Cameras Wireless Outdoor-2K Home Security Camera Battery Powered, Outdoor Security Cameras with 3MP Color Night Vision/Spotlight/IP66 Waterproof/PIR Detection/2-Way Talk/Cloud/SD

Betron EMR90 Foldable Wireless Bluetooth Headphones Over Ear with Microphone Mic Deep Bass There are fortunately many wireless headphones in this price range these days. Usually they are pretty similar, but this is one of the better ones. The first thing I noticed is how SOFT the ear cups are. It feels like something that belongs on a more expensive set, almost luxurious. That makes these much more comfortable to wear for long periods versus many of the other inexpensive headphones. The build quality feels good, and the sound quality is pretty decent too. Speakers of this size are usually pretty good at their bass response, and these are no exception. They naturally have a bit of noise isolation due to the cup design, and you have the option to connect a 3.5mm cable to use them as traditional wired headphones as well.
The one thing I DON'T like, is the microphone. Don't buy these for phone calls. The mic is too far from your mouth to separate you from background noises. Yes, I know airpods also have their mic far from your math but Apple has some sort of magic voodoo to make that work somehow. I've never liked the mic on any of these headphones, so I'm used to that by now. But I feel like these are marketed more for people who want to listen to music, and for that they are great and comfortable! I honestly wish they would disable the handsfree profile so that my phone wouldn't keep trying to use it for phone calls. Otherwise, a solid buy for this price!

Having a Galaxy Nexus phone, I felt quite comfortable with navigating and configuring the Nexus 7. It's very convenient to be able to share so many apps between my phone and this tablet. The Nexus 7 seems like it's very well built. It has just enough heft to not feel cheap, and the rubberized backing has a nice grip (though this won't matter to most, since a case will likely be the first accessory anyone buys.) The display is wonderful, and has quite a large viewing angle. For such small speakers, I'd say that the Nexus 7 sounds pretty good. I've only charged the device twice, since 12/24, and it gets used quite a bit.

So far, I've used the Nexus 7 for watching videos online (YouTube, Netflix, HBO Go,) streaming music from Amazon Prime, browsing the web, some light gaming with Final Fantasy Dimensions, chatting and computing (Maxima for Android and Wolfram Alpha) and I would say that it's handled everything I've thrown at it like a champ.

The only other tablet I own is a Kindle Fire HD 8.9", which works quite well for reading my technical PDFs, but seems to lack in the other "tablet" departments. I have used an iPad or two in the past. I would have to say that the Nexus 7 is by far my favorite tablet so far.

I'm currently using an Armorsuit screen protector and a Moko slim case that folds into a stand, and would recommend both accessories. I ordered a blue tooth keyboard. I'm hoping that the Nexus 7 with a keyboard might replace my aging netbook.

If I want a switch to turn off equipment, I often want to keep it off most of the time, so I want the light to be able to see it. On the other hand, if I keep the equipment on most of the time, then I don't need extra lights being powered (no matter how insignificant).

14AWG conductors and ground mean you can get the maximum out of most household circuits (because most are 15 amp). I don't like any extension cords or strips less than that to avoid voltage drop, overloading, etc.

Love the flat plug, especially for semi-permanent installations.

Wish the cord was more white considering my trim is white, but it's close enough to not annoy me in most cases.

Sound quality is clear, but very bass heavy. Unlike more better quality earbuds, these have no equalizer feature to help you get a more natural sound profile. Curiously, these earbuds do have the AAC CODEC for iPhones, but no aptX that Android phones prefer.

Noise cancellation is pretty good for this price range, though it does reduce your battery life somewhat. Battery life without noise cancellation is about average for the budget-price point, but not as good as what more expensive earbuds offer.

There is no wireless charging, though I'm not a huge fan of that anyway, especially for headphones.

I give 5 stars for OnePlus phone owners, but only 3.5 stars for everyone else.

A couple of notes. 1) it is possible to install the Google Play app store on this tablet, but the user interface is very clunky. Many of the Google Play apps work much better than what comes with the Amazon appstore, though. 2) you can install some apps to your SD card instead of main memory, but they then load more slowly. text_fidelity_a:
Echo Show 5 (1st Gen, 2019 release) -- Smart display with Alexa – stay connected with video calling - Charcoal (I have upgraded my review again to take off another star. This gadget is IMPOSSIBLE. You have to BELLOW at it to make it do anything. I am sorry I bought it, and the second one that we sent to my mother-in-law so we could talk face to face. Unfortunately, no one where she lived knew how to set it up and she died before we could set it up for her. So I basically wasted $145 for two Echo Shows because the one we have at home is no prize.)

(I have upgraded my review to take off a star. Since we have not been able to do face-to-face calling on it--no one where my MIL lives knows how to set it up--it basically is useless for the purpose we got it. Yeah, I loaded some photos on it so now I can look up and see our previous dog or a pic of my mom. But really, the old 2nd Generation Echo Dot responded better and more quickly. THIS THING IS DEAF. I used to be able to call up the stairs before I took the dog out "Echo, what's the temperature outside?" and like THAT I'd get a response. You have to bellow at the Show two or three times. Sometimes I have to stand right next to it to make it listen. But it loves my husband's voice and always responds. The drop-ins were crisp and clear on the Dot. It was a real waste of money.)

We had a bright idea: buy one of these for us, and buy one for my husband's mother, so we could video call her at any time (she lives 2 hours drive away), and his sister who lives in with his mom. Well, due to circumstances, we still haven't gotten the second Echo Show down to Mom, but are using the first one. Right now we are not making much use of the screen, save for a clock and a thermometer, but we have branched out into routines that are rather fun. We have tried out its video capabilities and that is very good, although we have trouble with backlighting from where our Show is placed.

I have two complaints about the Show: I think the voice is more muffled, and it doesn't seem as voice responsive as the Dot. If anything is running in the background, like the television or music, it gets really hard of hearing. We have to shout.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Show 5 (1st Gen, 2019 release) -- Smart display with Alexa – stay connected with video calling - Charcoal

12x42 Binoculars for Adults - HD Low Light Night Vision - Compact Lightweight (1.05lb) - Powerful BAK4 Prism FMC Lens - Waterproof Binoculars for Bird Watching, Hunting, Sports -Phone Adapter Included In this $30-50 price range, I think you should stick with this one. We got another one listed at $40 and besides for the branding, it seems to be the same binocular with slight molding differences. The tech is the same. Don't bother spending a little more unless you really want to upgrade and get one with zoom function. All these economy versions do not have zoom. And if you're new to binoculars, there is a learning curve, but this is how you focus:

1. Set the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial to ZERO and set sight on a distant subject. I'm not sure what zero means since there are no numbers, but there are arrows, so I presume it's when the arrows line up.

2. Cover the RIGHT FRONT lens with your hand, and rotate the FOCUSING WHEEL (the middle wheel), until the image is sharp. Keep both eyes open while you make this adjustment.

3. Now cover the LEFT FRONT lens and rotate the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial until the image is sharp. So here, you're not touching the focusing wheel, you're adjusting the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial.
text_fidelity_b: 12x42 Binoculars for Adults - HD Low Light Night Vision - Compact Lightweight (1.05lb) - Powerful BAK4 Prism FMC Lens - Waterproof Binoculars for Bird Watching, Hunting, Sports -Phone Adapter Included

ASUS N900 WiFi Router (RT-N66U) - Dual Band Gigabit Wireless Internet Router, 4 GB Ports, Gaming & Streaming, Easy Setup, Parental Control After searching review after review for a router with solid performance and features I ended up with the N66. I am not a networking professional but I can tell you there is an enormous difference between a good N900 router and an N300 router you may have gotten from your ISP. I would take any review that is not written by a professional with a grain of salt but here's my 2 cents.

I live in a densely populated area with 20+ Wi-Fi networks with decent strength AND I live in a brick building. I have 50 Mps/down from my ISP and with this router I am able maintain at least 50 Mps throughout my ~900 ft2 apartment with one exception, the back porch. Speeds dip to about 15 Mps on the back porch on both the 2.4 & 5 Ghz bands, as I understand it Wi-Fi doesn't get along with brick. There is a brick wall in between my the rest my house and and finally my router. Understandable.

The takeaway, if you need a fast router, I think you will be hard pressed to find a better one. I haven't even touched on USB support for printers, USB applications & external storage, VPN, iOS applications, etc.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS N900 WiFi Router (RT-N66U) - Dual Band Gigabit Wireless Internet Router, 4 GB Ports, Gaming & Streaming, Easy Setup, Parental Control

Aoybevty USB C to USB C 3.1/3.2 Cable 6FT, 10Gbps Data Transfer 100W Fast Charging 4K@60Hz Video Monitor Cable for Thunderbolt 4/3 Laptop Tablet Cell Phone USB Type C Electronics Devices This usb type-c to type-c cable is costs a little more than other cables you may see because it is not just a charging cable.

When it comes to the Type-C port, consumers now need to have a phd in electronics just to understand what works with what. There are just so many standards crammed into this reversible port that you need to really read the fine print to know whether it will work for your uses. What's worse is that once you throw these cables into a drawer, good luck finding the right one.

Type-C cables that come with your phone or phone charger will generally only be good for charging your phone, but not great for transferring data. This Type-C cable will carry up to 100w of power, meaning it will charge your phone or tablet at the highest speed it can support. When transferring data, this cable will allow you to copy files at the highest USB 3.1 speeds.

But more than that, this cable supports video signals so that it will be usable to connect your laptop or phone to a portable type-c monitor (assuming your devices support it).

Personally, I got this cable to work with a pair of NReal Air video glasses so that I have a backup to the cable included in the box. These cables work but are a little bit stiff.
text_fidelity_b: Aoybevty USB C to USB C 3.1/3.2 Cable 6FT, 10Gbps Data Transfer 100W Fast Charging 4K@60Hz Video Monitor Cable for Thunderbolt 4/3 Laptop Tablet Cell Phone USB Type C Electronics Devices

text_fidelity_a:
SIMOLIO 2.4G Analog Wireless TV Headsets with 100ft Transmit Range, No Pairing, No Delay, TV Voice Highlighting Headphones for Seniors, Wireless TV Headphones with Extra Soft Earbuds (SM-823 Pro) I began researching these based on reviewing another popular brand. I am a stickler for detail and after hours of research and asking questions I decided to give these a try because of the cost and positive reviews. I bought these for my elderly parent (90 years old) who has hearing loss but does not wear a hearing aid.
After a couple weeks of use I can honestly say these things are great! Very easy to install, easy to use for an elderly person not technically savvy, works from a long distance (we tried the next room), and the volume of these units can go very loud which is good for all types of hearing. There is also a balance control in case a person hears differently in both ears, and a switch to change from normal to higher or lower frequencies to help those with that type of hearing loss.
We can now watch TV when visiting my parent without the TV being so loud. But it is hard to verbally communicate with each other when they wear the headphones, but that’s not a big deal.
You can turn down the TV as low as needed, even muted, but the headphones can be as loud as needed. We used the RCA output from their TV (a 4 year old flat screen) and that works great. We tried it on a new flat screen and worked well also (digital output). All cables are provided along with extra ear inserts.
I like the fact this uses 2.4GHz instead of Bluetooth or infrared which often can lose connection with interference or movement away from the base station. I went out of the room into the next room and heard this one just fine.
The weight was a concern for me but my parent only watches TV for no more than 2 hours at the time and they said it was fine. There are ear loops provided to help with holding the unit if needed.
The only issue I found was that the input on the base station to charge the headphones was oriented backwards to how a person takes off the headset (have to turn the headset around to charge). And when putting on from the base station you have to turn the headphones around else you’ll put it on backwards which is not a big deal, but the volume button and balance will be reversed meaning my parent the first time turned the balance thinking it was volume and thought something was wrong. That’s one more thing for an elderly person to remember, plus you don’t need a lot of pressure to bend/break the charging prongs in the base unit if installed the wrong way.
We used the “speaker” option one time and it worked pretty well to allow a person to hear conversations in the room.

I’ll update this review should something change, but for now I highly recommend.

I unpacked it and noticed it feels cheaper, oh well, not the first manufacture to make a product from cheaper materials as time goes on...

But the strangest thing... the little nubs you use to position your fingers are on the wrong keys??? On the left hand, it's under your index finger on the F key as expected. But on the right hand, it's under my middle finger on the K key. Makes no sense to have them be under different fingers. The middle finger, index finger I don't care but make it the same on both sides.

I already threw my old one out, and I could get it out of the trash but I tossed the dongle in the trash too would never be able to find it again...

In the end, unless there is something you really like about this keyboard (for me it was an ergo keyboard with no number pad) I would consider something else.

text_fidelity_a:
PreSonus C3.5 BT Channel Studio Monitor I have been wanting to get a bluetooth speaker for connecting to my tablet for a while so I was very pleased to get an opportunity to try this speaker set. It is far and away better than what I originally had in mind and so far I am more than pleased with them.

Setup of these speakers is straightforward and simple, so much so that instructions really are not needed to get started. The wire connector is color-coded to make connecting the speakers to each other almost completely foolproof. If I have any complaints about the setup it would be that the wire connector is a little on the short side but that’s an easy fix - just buy longer wire.

I enabled bluetooth on my tablet, told the speaker set to make itself available and the tablet connected to it immediately. One could not ask for anything simpler. The process took less than a minute and most of that time was spent walking across the room to press the bluetooth button on the speakers.

I loaded up Pandora and told the tablet to play and almost immediately it was clear that these speakers are far above average. The sound profile is stunning - clear and crisp highs, rich midrange and very satisfying bass without overdriving. These speakers do an outstanding job of accurately reproducing the sound. On the back of the main (control) speaker there are two knobs for adjusting the highs and lows should the middle be unsatisfactory for some reason. These speakers also do a good job with spacial elements and there is depth to the sound.

I paired the speakers with my laptop (once I powered off the tablet) as well and it was also very easy.

I took some cables and wired the speakers to an older television in the house to see how much better watching TV would be. It was definitely better and it have a more spacial and stereo sound experience but with our TV this prevented us from making any volume adjustments unless we turned the volume knob on the speaker itself. This is a minor nuisance but certainly not a real issue.

In addition to great sound, these seem to be well-build and rugged, a good sign right out of the box. These are an excellent choice for a home theater system or an audiophile's listening room.

So far I have found nothing about which to complain with these speakers. Set-up is a snap and the sound quality is just amazing. These are speakers for the serious listener.
text_fidelity_b: PreSonus C3.5 BT Channel Studio Monitor

That keeps your fingerprints from the sticky side of the glass screen. Dab your device's screen with the blue sticky paper to be sure you removed all the dirt. Slide the triangular plastic piece over the indentation and it should give you a perfect seal over the device's screen.

It's beautiful.

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm FinePix J40 12.2 MP Digital Camera with 3x Optical Zoom and 3-Inch LCD (Includes 2 GB SD Memory Card) The camera is $[..]for gosh sakes! It's an amazing little piece of technology. The 3X optics and 12.2MP CMOS camera are well matched in the optical train to provide a great image for casual photos adequate for most users. It's the simplest start-up I've ever seen. The viewer LCD provides a maximum size to the package. `The manual' is 7 steps of which 4 include inserting memory, battery, charging battery and turning it on. It's `point and shoot' in the extreme.

I work in the domain of optics & imaging design. My wife has a 5 year old Fuji camera of this same genre that I've gone to some lengths to compare with Nikon and Canon in this low cost market. Without getting technical ... for the old Fuji, there are no user discernable image quality differences. The Fuji optics were superior (i.e. best objective lens light capture and transfer). Take your pick between the 3 on the backend image processing system/PC interface.

My wife has carried the 5 year old Fuji in her purse every day ... that's a technically demanding reliability challenge. Fuji can be relied on to deliver the best value for money in an image capture platform if you're designing a million dollar platform or this $69 platform. You're not paying the premium for the huge advertisement budget of Nikon and Canon when you buy Fuji. I think you just get a better camera.

I can't speak to this unit's reliability for now. A 3x optical train with autofocus, f-stop, etc mechanisms and micro motors are robust to a point. They will all fail, even the highest dollar product, if exposed to the wrong environment (g-shock, sand, salt spray, thermal shock, etc).

One reviewer mentioned software loading problems. I had absolutely no problems on a Windows 7, 64bit OS.

You can't go wrong with this device. It's an excellent camera for you or the kids or the g-kids for Xmas.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm FinePix J40 12.2 MP Digital Camera with 3x Optical Zoom and 3-Inch LCD (Includes 2 GB SD Memory Card)

APLOS Industrial Mini PC Powerful Intel Core i5-7267U Max Turbo Frequency 3.5Ghz Fanless Desktop Computer, 8GB RAM 256GB SSD WIN10 Pro OS, 6 x Gigabit Ethernet Network Firewall Gateway Router This is a very cool piece of computing hardware for specific uses. The fanless design means unlike other mini PCs that I've tried, this is actually silent! I'm surprised because the i5 CPU should generate more heat than the miserly Celeron that other mini PCs use, but the fins seems to dissipate heat rather well so far.
The 6 ethernet ports means this can make a pretty cool Windows-powered server for internet or file serving, and the fanless design means it can sit in a home users' closet and not make any audible noise either! While the CPU is pretty good, the GPU is pretty...not. If you look at the attached user benchmark, you'll see the CPU benched at about 74th percentile, but the GPU at a disappointing 4th percentile.
That means you won't really use this for things like games, not that anyone was expecting to. However, it does sort of limit this use for something like a media server using a platform such as Plex, as it would rely on the GPU for real-time media encoding.
For just playing back HD video it should be sufficient, and for other kinds of custom home server use and/or industrial use, this is a pretty interesting and useful product!

text_fidelity_a:
Arlo Pro - Wireless Home Security Camera System with Siren | Rechargeable, Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, 2-Way Audio, Wall Mount | Cloud Storage Included | 1 camera kit (VMS4130) UPDATE: After over a year of using these, I have to say that the bad outweighs the good, especially for how expensive they are.

It is true. There is nothing easier to set up. But it's next to useless when you actually need it. They trigger way too slowly. And the batteries are not set up to charge or even work very well when it's really cold out, so even though they are close enough to an outlet for me to charge them without taking them down, I have to bring them inside to charge them when it is cold. But it's the slow trigger that really makes this system not worth the expense.

For example: New Year's Eve, someone wrote Happy New Year in the snow on my windshield. One of my Arlo cameras is pointed right at my car. I have a clip from before it happened. I have a clip from after it happened. If I did not also have wired cameras that record continuously, I would not know whom to thank (our sweet next door neighbors - they are so lovely!).

The cameras make decent deterrents. And they are handy to have when I need a live view of something. But if you want to catch somebody doing something, there are better options.

_____________
Original Review Follows
_____________

I'm going to give you the bad, then the just okay, and then the good. Short version of all that is that I wish these triggered a bit faster and weren't so expensive, but they are a substantial improvement over my older Arlo system. Skip to the end if you want to know how to set up the siren.

Bottom line: This system is not quite perfect, and it is quite expensive, but it is wireless, weatherproof, super easy to set up, and backwards compatible. I would recommend this to a family member or anyone else who needs a wireless outdoor install.

Okay, so the bad (and it isn't really that bad) is that the Arlo Pro cameras have some trigger lag. Depending on how fast the trigger is moving, you may catch them just as they leave the frame, or you might miss them altogether. If it's a person walking, no problem. A person walking briskly? Might be a little problem. Basically, these are better for a zombie apocalypse than for a werewolf invasion. I have a hardwired CCTV DVR system that is always "recording," so when it gets a motion alert, it "starts" the clip five seconds in the past.

The just okay part is that, for this kind of money, I wish the cameras had more configurability. I would like to be able to set the exact parameters of the field I want to monitor (currently, you can pan and zoom but that's not really what I am looking to do), and I would like to be able to set the sensitivity in a meaningful way (I live in a city on a fairly busy street and get hundreds of alerts/clips no matter how I try to minimize them). Additionally, the over-sensitivity is a drain on battery life, which is an indirect functional limitation on where I install the cameras. With batteries needing to be changed/charged within a matter of days, I need to be able to get to these easily.

Now for the good stuff:

I like Arlo a lot. I have three of the old ones, and even with the lag, they are great for outdoor applications. The Arlo Pro cameras are better. The video quality is better. While there is lag, it is not as bad as it is on the older models. These are also BY FAR the easiest cameras to set up and keep running. I have wifi range extenders throughout my weird old condo, and my Arlo cameras never drop their signals.

The Arlo Pro base station will work with your old Arlo cameras. I kept my old base station running, though, so that I can run different cameras on different schedules. It also works with IFTTT and with the Smart Things App.

The Siren was not intuitive to set up, but it is a cool feature. The default is OFF for all cameras, so don't worry about setting it off while you are setting your system up. You activate it in the settings of each camera - camera by camera. You can also trigger it from the smart phone app, so in the event that someone breaks in while you are home, you can turn on the alarm (better for a werewolf invasion than for the zombie apocalypse).

From the Arlo website:
To create a rule that includes a siren trigger:
Launch the Arlo app or log in to your Arlo account at arlo.netgear.com.
Tap or click Mode to access the mode tab.
Tap or click the Arlo Pro base station for which you would like to add a siren trigger.
Tap the pencil icon or click > next to the mode that you would like to edit.
Under Rules, tap the pencil icon or click Edit next to the device that you want to trigger the siren.
Select the Turn Siren ON check box.
Tap the pencil icon or click > next to Turn Siren ON.
Set the sliders for Siren Duration and Siren Loudness.
Tap < Edit Rule or click Back.
Tap Done or click Save.
Note: This rule is not active until you activate the mode to which you added the siren trigger.
text_fidelity_b: Arlo Pro - Wireless Home Security Camera System with Siren | Rechargeable, Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, 2-Way Audio, Wall Mount | Cloud Storage Included | 1 camera kit (VMS4130)

text_fidelity_a: Jabra SUPREME Driver's Edition Bluetooth Headset - Retail Packaging - Black/Silver Since the [[ASIN:B009S4FMB6 Jabra SUPREME Driver's Edition Bluetooth Headset - Retail Packaging - Black/Silver]] comes with a headband, I tend to use it with the headband.  Unfortunately, my hair is thinning because I lose some each time I remove the headset.  Regardless, this bluetooth is extremely easy to synch with my Droid and it's recognized each and every time I turn on the Bluetooth in the car.  I wear this only for driving and I don't care that passersby give me funny looks, it works great.  The earpiece is larger than most contemporary bluetooth devices, but it's cushiony and comfortable for long drives.  The microphone is sensitive and responsive.  I haven't had a complaint yet with any call.  Slipping the earphone onto the headband is a simple task, and I find that I'm wearing it 90% of the time, preferring that to the ear wire and no band.  My main criticism other than the hair pulling of this design is that it takes some getting used to to operate the touch controls as well as turn the device on and off.  When off of the band, it's an easy feat, but no so when it's attached and you can't bend the microphone down completely.  Since the battery is really long lasting, it hasn't run out of power yet in the middle of a call.  Because you have options for charging this set, you're a step ahead, and with an adjustable headband, it fits most head sizes.  It's a good set.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra SUPREME Driver's Edition Bluetooth Headset - Retail Packaging - Black/Silver

Everyone agreed that this screen cleaner did an excellent job on small screens, like phones and tablets. I found that it wasn't as good on larger screens though. On 1920x1080 full size desktop screens, the cleaner was more awkward to use and  was more prone to streaking and such. One nice thing though is that the spray had no chemical smell. In fact, it didn't have any discernible odor at all. Our techie teen figured out how to get the bottle out so it can be refilled when necessary. I did have a little trouble figuring out how the stand work and I wondered why a screen cleaner needed an attached stand. As it turns out, I'm glad it has one. It works very nicely for my 10" tablet. The family consensus was to give this product a 4 star rating because it worked so well on small screens and because the stand actually turned out to be useful. The fact that it was less effective on larger screens and that it is a bit pricey are the reasons it didn't get a full 5 stars. Our family liked this screen cleaner. It just didn't quite make it to the top rating.

text_fidelity_a:
co2CREA Hard Case with Sleep Mode Replacement for Apple AirPods Max Headphone (Black Case + Inside Red) First, mine didn’t smell.

Now that I have the positive attributes out of the way let’s discuss why you should avoid this case.
I reluctantly paid $33 for this and I have to wonder what I was thinking. It’s nowhere near worth that much.

It will not/cannot survive a side impact. Well that’s not true. It cannot protect your APM from a hit or drop that could damage them from the top. I’m not sure if it could from the bottom or sides. It’s either molded cardboard or thin plastic covered with fabric. No padding, just fabric.

Internally there is another layer of cardboard (or plastic, thin, very thin) covered in a felt like material. There’s absolutely no drop protection.

The magnets designed to put the APM into “sleep” mode lay flat. You will have to pinch them up while putting your headphones into it if you wish to keep them from clanging together and not using the stock case. Even then the magnets don’t work every time. See my pic.

Overall this is a $10 case marked up cause they can. I mean we have expensive headphones so why not charge us more? We have already proven we will pay.

Skip this thing. Mine is going back. If you want something to protect them in a backpack then still look elsewhere. You can get something equal to this for less.

Thanks for your time.
text_fidelity_b: co2CREA Hard Case with Sleep Mode Replacement for Apple AirPods Max Headphone (Black Case + Inside Red)

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm X-E2 16.3 MP Mirrorless Digital Camera with 3.0-Inch LCD - Body Only (Silver) I've only had the Fujifilm X-E2 camera and 18-55mm lens for a short while and I've barely scratched the surface of it's capabilities. This is a camera anyone can use right out of the box but also one that you can spend years learning to master.

The retro look and styling are very attractive but they made it, for me at least who was used to an extended grip on the camera body, a little hard to handle. I found myself hitting the AE-L and AF-L buttons often and frequently by accident spun the exposure compensation dial without even realizing I had. I resolved this with the LensMate Thumb Grip designed for the X-E1/E2. It made a good camera great. I also added LensMate's brass soft release button to the shutter release. It does aid in smoother pressing of the shutter button but it also looks great on the camera.

The 18-55mm lens that comes with the X-E2 is a real pleasure to use. The zoom is stiff enough to let you feel in control but easy enough that you don't need brute force to use it.

Image quality, even at 100%, is outstanding. I've been getting so many 'keepers' that I've had to reevaluate my shooting style. I feel like I'm overshooting. In the past I was shooting three or four hundred images in an outing and getting maybe four or six shots I really want to keep and share. Now, with the X-E2 I'm finding two, three even four times that many shots that are worth keeping. I'm going to need a bigger hard drive!

Battery life has been pretty good for me. Even shooting in temperatures down in the 30's and 40's I had no problem taking well over three hundred images and still having battery bars left. In the times I've gone out all day wandering around the county I've yet to have to swap out the battery though I did purchase an extra just to have around.

Functionality, configurability and controls are extensive and a bit quirky but easy enough to get used to. As an example the Q button gives you 'Q'uick access to many of the more necessary and often used controls. You navigate around the Q menu with the 5-way controller but you make setting changes with the command dial. One of the features I found most interesting was the ability to constrain the ISO in Auto mode and set a minimum shutter speed. I also liked the ability to configure the four letter prefix for file names. All the 'extra' settings like special effects, double exposure, movie mode and panorama are accessed through the Drive button.

I did find a couple small negatives. Nothing to cause me not to want to use it but made me wonder. The odd menu systems. The pop-up flash is a bit anemic and is somewhat blocked by the 18-55mm lens. It's even worse when the hood is attached. The shoulder strap that comes with the camera... I know they're usually bad but this is cheap camera bad not quality camera bad. I put it around my neck, gave a tug, and then threw it away without putting it on the camera. I expected a little more quality there. The tulip lens hood that comes with the 18-55mm feels hard and brittle. It too could have been a bit better quality. I already mentioned the LensMate thumb grip that I think is an absolute must add item (it's really worth the cost). My big clumsy hands desperately needed it to aid in stability and control.

Where to start with a conclusion? This is an interesting mix of old school retro styling and modern camera technology. I think Fuji have really blended them together well. I can see myself enjoying this camera for years to come. Very highly recommended.

{Update}
Not wanting to pile on the negatives but I had intended to and completely forgot to mention the battery door. It's really kind of flimsy and feels like it could easily break. Also, with the way it's hinged I find it rather hard to get the memory card out of the camera because it's so close and parallel to the battery door's hinge.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm X-E2 16.3 MP Mirrorless Digital Camera with 3.0-Inch LCD - Body Only (Silver)

Rii I8 Mini 2.4Ghz Wireless Touchpad Keyboard With Mouse For Pc, Pad, Xbox 360, Ps3, Google Android Tv Box, Htpc, Iptv (Black) When my review sample arrived I tested it on a few devices and it worked perfectly on each. The first device was my ancient ThinkPad T61 running Windows XP. I inserted the dongle (look in the battery compartment for it), and it was immediately recognized and activated. As soon as I turned on power to the keyboard I was able to navigate using the touchpad, bring up an editor and type.

The next tests were with my [[ASIN:B00JA5DCNS Keedox® Quad Core RK3188 Android 4.2 1080P 5G 2.4G HDMI Bluetooth 4.0 Smart TV BOX]], then using a [[ASIN:B00C7SK2J2 Micro USB OTG Host Cable to USB 2.0]] I connected the dongle to my Galaxy Note 3 phone and Tab 3 10.1 tablet respectively and was texting and performing other functions. This is truly a plug-and-play keyboard/touchpad.

One final thing I love is the battery is a standard BT51 that can be purchased just about anywhere if you are such a power user that you need a spare.

It's set up for thumb style texting, so most folks will be immediately comfortable with it. I love the tactile feedback from the keys, which were a pleasure to type with, as well as the array of function keys and buttons. If you spend a lot of time on smaller devices this is a dream come true. At about thirteen bucks at the time of this review it's a bargain for folks who are heavy texters.

text_fidelity_a:
Cyber Acoustics Stereo USB Headset (AC-5008A), in-line Controls for Volume & Mic Mute, Adjustable Mic Boom for PC & Mac, Perfect for Classroom or Home This headset does cancel noise, and the sound is clear. That part is fine. For the not-so-fine parts: they're really tight, and they cancel noise almost too well.

The tightness:
Right away, I felt that they squeezed my ears too much. I left them to stretch across several hard-bound books for a few days which loosened them up for a while, but they eventually go back to their original tightness that I can't wear them for more than 15 minutes at a time. My ears get squashed and they hurt to leave on, and I don't even have a big melon head!

The noise-cancelling:
While they do block out outside noise, they cancel my own voice out too, and I feel like I'm talking into a blanket by myself - I can barely hear myself talk. It's very disconcerting.

All in all, if they weren't so darn tight, I think I'd like them better. I had to dock 1.5 stars because of the physical discomfort, and .5 star for the talking-into-an-echoless-void factor. The sound quality is good, though. So, if you have a smallish head, and you like having all the outside sound shut out, they may work for you.
text_fidelity_b: Cyber Acoustics Stereo USB Headset (AC-5008A), in-line Controls for Volume & Mic Mute, Adjustable Mic Boom for PC & Mac, Perfect for Classroom or Home

The system that allows remote viewing is unable to reboot itself when power is restored, so if your home loses power for some reason while you are not home, the sync Module does not automatically reconnect when the power comes back on. My original system, Zmodo does air reconnect so if my home loses power, the cameras reconnect as soon as they have power again. In fact the cameras were what alerted us to the return of power to our home during the 2016 fires in Napa. I will stick with them, despite the wiring issue. They are just more reliable.

text_fidelity_a:
Targus Demolition Backpack Designed to Fit up to 17.3-Inch Laptop, Black (TSB220US) I was able to do a direct comparison between this and the SwissGear SA1908 ScanSmart Backpack. And it turns out that deciding which pack to grab on the way out is surprisingly one of the hardest decisions one could have to make. Both packs are obviously of the best quality with a similar nylon shell, strong stitching, and smooth zippers. Both are designed to fit 17" laptops and have similar interior volumes, and yet the features vary widely. Let's have a look at key points:

-The Targus is perfect for a user carrying a laptop and a tablet and/or Kindle. In front of the laptop compartment is a soft fabric lined pocket to hold a tablet against the laptop and protect the screen from scratches. The very front pocket is also soft with a piece of padding that fits the newest Kindle nicely.

-The SwissGear may be better for carrying just a laptop or two laptops. It has the ScanSmart feature, which is great when TSA allows it to work (sometimes they make you remove your computer anyway, either out of ignorance or their suspicion that you packed incorrectly for it to work - that makes it easier just to remove it sometimes rather than risk a fight with them). And I often store a second laptop in the ScanSmart opening.

-I love that on the Targus, the zipper pulls for the main compartment and the two side compartments can be placed between the bag and your back, thwarting casual thieves. As an extremely paranoid person, this gives extra peace of mind. For that matter, I really like the unique design of these pockets. The side pockets can be really useful, and the big compartment can be accessed from a larger opening. But that uniqueness comes at a cost...

-...and that cost is the looks. I didn't like the looks on the picture, but then it grew on me. In person, I don't really like it that much, but it might be growing on me. I guess the tradeoff is simple: you get a very unique design that works great and you get some serious padding for your electronics and some extra comfortable straps, but that all equals a slightly awkward looking pack. It's not too bad, but I think an accent color would go a long way. In contrast, the SwissGear under observation is quite beautiful and more traditional, yet not as padded or protected.

-The Targus came in a very thin box. It has a semi-rigid pad on the bottom that can fold up to flatten it out or fold down and attach with velcro to add some structure to the main compartment. This is also a very smart feature.

-The SwissGear has a phone/MP3 player holder with earphone exit, for those interested. That's not the best one I've ever seen though, as it is only a hanging cradle for the device.

-The Targus has more padding, while the SwissGear has a better airflow system for your back.

Conclusion: I really love both of these backpacks, and I'm surprised how different two top notch backpacks can be. I can see how the designers have to pick and choose the features they want to incorporate, because you really just can't have it all without making the pack bigger, and I wouldn't want that. They both deserve five stars, absolutely. The Targus strikes me as the pack for someone serious about the transportation and protection of their electronics, or anyone else who is intrigued to try this unique, excellent design.
text_fidelity_b: Targus Demolition Backpack Designed to Fit up to 17.3-Inch Laptop, Black (TSB220US)

text_fidelity_a:
TomTom XL 350 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator The good:

Lane guidance. I like to plan my turns and exits, especially in thick traffic. I hate it when the passenger who claims to know the way suddenly says "Left turn here!" to feet from the intersection when I'm in the right lane and the middle and left lanes are packed with traffic. No more. Tom Tom says things like, "Take a right on 17th street, then a left on Maritime Road, giving me time to get into that left lane." It also gives you lane guidance for exiting the highway, when it's right two lanes for this highway, and middle two for this bridge and left one for the other bridge. You can see on screen, and it tells you aloud, which land you want.

It tells you "left turn here", which is good when the street sign is missing or obscured.

It adapts quickly. It seems to know traffic laws, so it doesn't try to put you the wrong way on a one way the way Mapquest did in the early days.

It tracks your speed.

The route chosen to a familiar location surprised me, but thinking it over, it was the most direct route. I normal go one exit on the highway. It had me go a few very small side streets instead.

It works in or out of the car, for those who want to use it for camping or geocaching.

The bad:

Even on the loudest setting, it's a little hard to hear. The pronunciation is off, which one might expect, but the volume is poor. It's hard to hear, even with no one talking in the car. Good luck if you've got kids in the back seat.

It was a little hard to figure out. It wants the street then the number, and I tried offering the full address. Once I figured it out, it was pretty easy and did a great job.
text_fidelity_b: TomTom XL 350 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator

text_fidelity_a:
PIONEER Truly Wireless in-Ear Headphones, Black, SE-C8TW(B) If you're an iphone user, you're probably wondering whether to buy these Pioneer wireless headphones or the Apple version. The Pioneer price is about 1/3 cheaper than Apple. The Pioneer earbuds fit in your ear, so you get much better sound and much better sound isolation. These are nowhere near as detailed or loud as similarly priced wired headphones, but that's true of all wireless Bluetooth earbuds. I will say the connection is stable and not noisy, so these are better than most cheap Bluetooth earbuds. There is some bass, but don't work well for bass-heavy music. Maximum volume is just OK. Battery life is only about 3 hours per charge (compared to 5 hours for Apple), then you have to put the earbuds back in the case for a 1 hour charge. 3 hours may be enough for you; you have to decide, but 5 hours is certainly going to be more interesting to most people. The charging case is much larger than the Apple charging case. The case is 3.3 inches long and 2.2 inches wide. These case is to big to fit comfortably in my pants pocket, so I would only carry it with me in a backpack or purse.

Usage is pretty simple. They paired easily with my phone as a normal Bluetooth device. The buttons on the headphones are easy to use. They are comfortable in my ears. They are secure enough so far, never feeling like they are going to fall out. They are not noticeably heavy like some earbuds can be. When in my ears, they are much less ugly than the Apple earbuds.

I would give these 5 stars for the price and performance if the sound and battery life were better. Frankly, I've tried a few different totally wireless earbuds and been less than impressed by all of them. Bluetooth headphones that have a wire connecting the two pieces can be had for much lower prices and have much better sound quality and much better battery life. Removing the wire just doesn't seem worth the downsides to me.
text_fidelity_b: PIONEER Truly Wireless in-Ear Headphones, Black, SE-C8TW(B)
